P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Event logging at scale (every action). Async logging prevents blocking.
P.P2_defensibility: Comprehensive audit trail. User can review history. Transparency.
P4_failure_modes: Event logging fails silently → history incomplete (mitigate: async with retry, alerts on repeated failures)
P.P5_backup_plan: If logging fails: queue async retry. Never block user action.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Test async logging under load. Test database failure handling.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Integration tests for logging all event types. Load tests for concurrent logging (100k/s).
P.P8_benchmarks: Event logging: <500ms (async). History retrieval: <1s for 1000 events.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial placeholder CONFolder for history MODULE

L.L1_legal_considerations: Audit trail for compliance. Retention policy for privacy (delete old events).
L.L4_liability_notes: History transparency builds user trust. Over-retention violates privacy.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Event storage: ~500B per event. At 100k users with 10 events/day: ~500MB/day = 180GB/year.
F.F2_accounting_considerations: Storage cost grows. Archive old events.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Events logged securely. Privacy events (location access) logged for transparency.
S.S2_data_privacy: User can see own history. Retention policy limits old events.
S.S4_access_control: User sees own history. Admin sees only for support.

X.X1_notes: Event history provides transparency and enables analytics. Helping reputation prevents gaming (track actual help given/received).
X2_open_questions: Event taxonomy: what events to log? (all actions, or filtered?)
Reputation algorithm: how to weight help events? (prevents fraud)
X.X3_related_research: Event logging systems. Audit trails. Reputation algorithms in peer-to-peer platforms.
